title: Rav Rechumi (I)

paragraphs: (Rechum, Ezra 2:2.) He was a student of Abaye and Rava, as in Nazir 13a, where he asked Abaye, and Pesachim 39a, where he raised a difficulty against Abaye.

Ketubot 62b relates his death: Rav Rechumi used to be before Rava in Mechoza and would regularly come home every eve of Yom Kippur. One day the teaching drew him on. His wife was waiting: “Now he is coming, now he is coming.” He did not come; she was distressed, and a tear fell from her eye. He was sitting on the roof; the roof collapsed beneath him and he died.
He is mentioned in Eruvin 14b: “Rav Rechumi teaches it thus: Rav Yehudah son of Rav Shmuel bar Shilat said in Rav’s name.”

notes.text: Saved Davidson Eruvin14b explicitly has Rav Yehudah son of Rav Shmuel [bar Shilat]. The former Yochanan/Shimon expansions are corrected, without a global rule for these abbreviations.

The consulted Eruvin 14b explicitly has Rav Rechumi reporting Rav Yehudah son of Rav Shmuel [bar Shilat]. The brackets around bar Shilat are those of this consulted edition. The separate teacher and death-narrative claims are retained as Hyman’s account.
